summary_html: Agency places a child with **relatives or kin caregivers** instead of non-relative foster care. Federal law favors kinship care as least-restrictive, family-preserving placement.

key_cases.case_name: S.R.B.R. v. Harrison County Department of Human Services
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed a family court's termination of parental rights, holding that the petitioner must prove at least one of the grounds enumerated in Section 93-15-103(3) by clear and convincing evidence.
key_cases.relevance: The children had lived since 1998 with an aunt and uncle who the guardian ad litem recommended as adoptive parents, the standard Mississippi kinship-to-permanency path.
key_cases.quote: the petitioner must prove by clear and convincing evidence at least one of the grounds enumerated

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed an award of custody to third-party custodians over the natural father, holding that the presumption favoring a natural parent is overcome by a clear showing of unfitness.
key_cases.relevance: Sets the showing a non-parent caregiver must make before custody is placed with them rather than the parent.
key_cases.quote: it has been stated many times that this presumption can be overcome by a clear showing that the parent is unfit

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the award of custody to the natural father over the maternal grandmother and declined to change the established grounds for rebutting the natural-parent presumption.
key_cases.relevance: Kinship placement cannot displace a fit parent absent abandonment, desertion, immoral conduct or unfitness proved by clear and convincing evidence.
key_cases.quote: we find no legally compelling reason to alter or abandon our established standards for rebuttal of the natural-parent presumption

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that ICWA Section 1912(d)'s remedial-efforts requirement applies only where termination would precipitate the breakup of an Indian family, and that Section 1912(f) and the Section 1915(a) placement preferences did not bar this adoption by a non-Indian couple.
key_cases.relevance: Holds Section 1915(a)'s placement preferences inapplicable where no alternative Indian family has formally sought to adopt, which constrains tribal kinship-placement claims.
key_cases.quote: Consistent with the statutory text, we hold that §1912(d) applies only in cases where an Indian family’s “breakup” would be precipitated by the termination of the parent’s rights.

key_cases.case_name: In the Matter of the Dissolution of the Marriage of Leverock and Hamby: Pendleton v. Leverock
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the chancellor's refusal to terminate the father's parental rights but reversed the award of custody to him, holding the record established desertion so that the natural-parent presumption was rebutted and custody had to be redetermined through an on-the-record Albright best-interests analysis.
key_cases.relevance: The leading modern Mississippi statement of what a third-party or in loco parentis caregiver must show - abandonment, desertion or other unfitness by clear and convincing evidence - before a child can be placed with them over a natural parent.
key_cases.quote: This presumption in favor of a natural parent has long been recognized, and Tony is entitled to it unless there is proof that he has relinquished it.
